thread:
Incident-Bot: PAGER -> High tail latency and increased 5xxs for tenant NimbusCorp (dedicated pool dp-7). Alert: 95p latency > 2s, error rate spiking to ~18%. Dashboard: https://console.redwood.io/alerts/INC-1895432100 :rotating_light:
Alex M.: I'm on it. Any idea if this is degraded hardware or scheduler backlog?
Jasmin K.: Seeing sustained queue depth on nimbus-queue. backlog=~380 requests, avg batch token use pegged at max_batch_tokens. Many long-context requests.
Mike O.: Confirmed. dp-7 nodes hitting continuous batching saturation; KV cache warmup low. Likely bespoke tenant workload: lots of long prompts that force big batches; scheduler is waiting to fill.
Elaine S.: Customer Slack (Nimbus) says some requests are timing out and some partial outputs are returned. They call this impacting their support automation.
Alex M.: We should avoid making things worse by increasing batch windows. Immediate idea: lower max_batch_tokens and increase concurrent batches so smaller batches go out quicker. Also consider temporarily pinning to a lower-ram model variant for long requests.
Jasmin K.: Agreed. Suggested interim knobs: max_batch_tokens: 768 (was 2048), max_concurrent_batches: 6 (was 3), batch_timeout_ms: 50 (was 100). This should reduce queueing tail but may increase tokens/sec.
Mike O.: Good call. Also enable tenant-specific prefix caching for common prefixes to reduce effective token generation. We can flip cache for tenant nimbus-queue: cache_policy=prefix-kv, ttl=1h.
Alex M.: I'll push scheduler change to dp-7 for tenant NimbusCorp now. Command:
```
# apply scheduler knobs to tenant
redwoodctl scheduler update --tenant=nimbus-corp --pool=dp-7 \
  --knobs '{"max_batch_tokens":768,"max_concurrent_batches":6,"batch_timeout_ms":50}'
```
Alex M.: Executing. Rolling to nodes in dp-7 (canary 2 nodes -> full).
Ops-Bot: Rollout started: rollout_id=r-202303-18954, canary nodes 2/2, expected full in ~90s. Logs will stream to /var/log/redwood/rollouts/r-202303-18954.log
Jasmin K.: After canary applied: 95p latency dropped from ~2.4s to ~1.3s on canary nodes, errors down from 18% -> 6%.
Mike O.: Continue to monitor. We might see overall throughput drop ~10-15% due to smaller batches; that's acceptable for availability.
Elaine S.: I'm going to message Nimbus support with ETA and mitigation note: "We've applied a scheduler tuning to reduce tail latency; monitoring for stabilization. If you still see partial outputs, use shorted prompts or request retries."
Alex M.: Also turned on prefix KV caching for tenant: command executed: `redwoodctl cache enable --tenant=nimbus-corp --policy=prefix-kv --ttl=3600`
Ops-Bot: Cache enable accepted, warming started on dp-7 nodes. Warm percent: 0% -> 45% in 2m.
Jasmin K.: Metrics now: 95p=1.02s, p50=180ms, error% ~3.2. Queue depth down to ~70. Looks stable but still recovering KV warm.
Mike O.: Proposed follow-up: keep knobs for 30 minutes, then evaluate. If tail resurges, plan B is immediate model fallback for requests >2048 tokens: route to openlm-small-qlora (lower memory, faster). Need product signoff for routing change.
Elaine S.: Acknowledged, will coordinate with product if needed. I'm standing by to take handoff at 18:00. Leaving runbook snippet in incident doc: step 1- check queue, step 2- confirm rollout success, step 3- watch cache warm %, step 4- if errors >5% re-evaluate knobs, step 5- consider model fallback.
Alex M.: Handoff note for evening oncall (Elaine): Current status: knobs applied, KV cache warming, latency improved significantly. Keep the tenant knobs in place for 30m, then gradually revert max_concurrent_batches to 4 if throughput becomes too low.
Elaine S.: Got it. I'll take over monitoring and contact Nimbus account team if anything regresses. Leaving a small test script for checking health:
```
# simple health check against nimbus queue
for i in {1..20}; do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.io/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ONCALL_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"tenant":"nimbus-corp","prompt":"hello","max_tokens":32}' | jq .status; sleep 1; done
```
Alex M.: Thanks, Elaine. Marking this thread as monitoring/resolved-for-now. I'll update incident doc with timeline.
Incident-Bot: ALERT update -> Incident state: mitigated (monitoring). If error rate re-spikes above 8% or queue depth >200 within next 45m, incident will auto-escalate. :white_check_mark:
